text:
ashley: raising an escalation — acme-inc reporting 504s on hosted inference /v1/generate starting ~10:20 UTC. multiple customers say requests time out around 40-60s.
kevin: oncall. looking now. any alert details?
ops-bot: ALERT: hosted-gpu-east-1 - 5xx rate spike 5m avg=18% | latency p95=1.2s -> 42s | new pods pending 12 | tags: autoscale
maria: I can see HPA + KEDA firing scale events, but a lot of new pods stuck in ContainerCreating/Init for ~90-150s. kube events show image pull and then long time in readiness.
samir: runtime logs from the service show repeated: `ERROR stream: connection timed out after 45s` and `warn: model weights not in kv cache, loading full model` — weight load times on GPU are 30-60s for this model. likely warmup not happening.
ashley: customer repro: they POST with 8 simultaneous short requests -> first few fail with 504, retries succeed after ~2m.
kevin: paste kubectl snippets?
maria: here — truncated: 
```
kubectl get pods -l app=inference -o wide
NAME                         READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
inference-6f7b9c5c6-abc1     0/1     ContainerCreating  0          2m
inference-6f7b9c5c6-def2     1/1     Running            0          8m
inference-6f7b9c5c6-ghi3     0/1     ContainerCreating  0          1m
```
and describe: 
```
Events:
  Type    Reason     Age    From               Message
  ----    ------     ----   ----               -------
  Normal  Pulling    2m     kubelet            Pulling image "redwood/inference-runtime:prod"
  Normal  Pulled     2m     kubelet            Successfully pulled image
  Normal  Created    2m     kubelet            Created container
  Warning Unhealthy  1m30s  kubelet            Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 504
```
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /healthz
    port: 8080
  initialDelaySeconds: 5
  periodSeconds: 10
  failureThreshold: 3

samir: initialDelaySeconds=5 is too small for GPU model load. pod becomes ready but the runtime still loading weights -> requests hit gateway and time out while backend is not warmed. Also KEDA's trigger config: cooldownPeriod is 30s and pollingInterval 30s. scaling from 2 -> 12 takes too long.
ashley: KEDA ScaledObject (excerpt):
```
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: inference-scaledobject
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    name: inference-deployment
  pollingInterval: 30
  cooldownPeriod: 30
  minReplicaCount: 2
  maxReplicaCount: 20
  triggers:
  - type: prometheus
    metadata:
      serverAddress: http://prometheus:9090
      metricName: inference_queue_length
      threshold: "100"
```
maria: so two problems: 1) readiness probe is too aggressive/short -> pod may be considered not ready while load still in-progress, or conversely it reports ready too early if check only returns 200 before full warmup. 2) KEDA/HPA tuning -> polling/cooldown cause slow reaction.
kevin: temporary mitigation options?
samir: we can: 
- bump minReplicaCount to 4 for the affected model to reduce coldstarts
- increase KEDA polling/prefetch so it scales faster (pollingInterval -> 10s, cooldown -> 90s?) actually cooldown should be higher to avoid flapping; pollingInterval lower to respond faster.
- change readinessProbe.initialDelaySeconds to 60 for GPU-backed models or make probe query runtime readiness (weights loaded flag)
- add a warmup init container that preloads/warms model weights before readiness true
- route traffic to Dedicated pool or fallback model variant smaller/quantized while scaling finishes

ashley: temporary customer update drafted: "We're seeing autoscaling delays causing cold starts and timeouts. We're increasing minimum capacity for your model and tuning autoscaler; will update when stabilized." cc: @jules
jules (acme-inc): appreciate quick response, this is hitting their production checkout flow. SLAs impacted.
kevin: I've bumped minReplicaCount to 4 for acme's model in the east cluster and enabled fallback routing to smaller model. watching metrics.
ops-bot: ACTION: deployed scaledobject change for inference-deployment (pollingInterval=10) by kevin.
support-bot: Ticket #12345 updated: status -> investigating; customer notified.
maria: follow-up checks: watch kube pod startups, kubelet logs show GPU driver load taking ~20-40s after container start; that plus model load hits 60-90s. need readiness to wait on runtime signal not just http 200.
samir: repro steps I used: 
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"prompt":"short"}' 
2) in parallel run 10 requests from a single client
3) observe 4-5 requests 504 within first 60s, subsequent requests succeed as pods become ready

logs captured: 
```
2026-07-12T10:21:45Z runtime INFO preloading model weights shard 0/8
2026-07-12T10:22:05Z runtime INFO model weights load complete
2026-07-12T10:22:30Z proxy ERROR upstream read timeout (client waited 45s)
```
ashley: owners + next steps:
- samir (eng-runtime): add explicit readiness endpoint that waits for KV cache ready & weights loaded; propose change and perf test.
- maria (eng-sre): run KEDA/HPA tuning playbook, validate with blast tests, set blue/green for scaledobject rollout.
- kevin (oncall): monitor and escalate if retries > 2% during next 30m, coordinate customer comms.
- support-bot: update ticket with actions and ETA 2h.

kevin: current status — error rate dropped to ~3% after bumping minReplicaCount + fallback; tracing shows fewer ContainerCreating stuck beyond 30s. keeping this thread open for postmortem.
ashley: customer updated. they asked for postmortem and whether this could hit other customers. we should schedule a quick RCA.
ops-bot: NOTE: scheduled follow-up runbook task created (#6789) to add GPU warmup probe and update templates for GPU-backed deployments.
samir: I'll prototype readiness change today and open PR with a small warmup init container + readiness check. will include perf numbers.
ashley: thanks all — closing escalation once we have a postmortem & PR linked. :thumbsup:
